transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Um... well, my sister actually made me come in. It's just that my body feels completely out of my control lately. Like, at first, I was pacing around my apartment all night, just constantly walking back and forth making all these notes for a supper club I want to start. I'm a waiter right now, but I took some business classes in college, and I realized there's this huge untapped market for underground dining. I was going to source all the ingredients locally, like from this farmer's market on 4th street—they have these amazing heirloom tomatoes, though honestly the parking over there is a complete nightmare on weekends, they really need to figure out the zoning. 

But anyway, I was pacing and planning all of that. And then... I don't know, lately I'm just so slowed down. Like, physically heavy. My sister was getting so mad at me this morning because she says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on. I just sat on the edge of the bed staring at the laces for I don't even know how long.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?

Hearing things? No, not really. I mean, my apartment building is super old, so the pipes make this weird groaning noise sometimes, but that's just the plumbing. My landlord is terrible about fixing it. His name is Gary, and he always promises he'll send a guy out, but he never does. Gary actually drives this vintage Corvette, which is wild because he won't spend a dime on the building, but he keeps that car pristine. I saw him waxing it last Tuesday when I was walking back from my shift at the restaurant. We had a huge lunch rush that day because the convention center down the street was hosting some big dental conference. Dentists tip surprisingly well, by the way. I guess they have a lot of disposable income. But, um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, seeing things. No, I don't see anything that isn't there. Just normal stuff. Just staring at my shoelaces, mostly.
During that time when you were pacing and making all those plans, did you feel unusually high or euphoric?

Yeah, I mean... actually, this was right after I got fired from my last job. Which was completely unfair, by the way. My manager, Brenda, said I was "disruptive," but honestly, she was just threatened because I suggested a total overhaul of the seating chart. She's been there for like fifteen years and still uses this ridiculous laminated paper system. It's so outdated. You can get an iPad app for like twenty bucks a month that tracks table turnover, but she wouldn't listen. She wears these really loud, clunky bracelets that jingle every time she points at something, and it used to drive me insane when I was trying to take orders. 

But anyway, yeah, after she let me go, I didn't even care. I felt weirdly unstoppable, you know? Like, super excited. I had all these ideas, like the supper club, and I just felt amazing. But the thing was, if anyone tried to tell me to slow down—like my sister did—or if they questioned my plans, I would just completely lose it. I'd blow up at them. It felt like they were actively trying to ruin my life and hold me back from doing something huge. My sister actually cried one night because I yelled at her for telling me to go to sleep. She always uses these lavender essential oils before bed, and the smell was just drifting into the hallway while I was trying to map out my business plan, and it was so distracting... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right. Yeah, I felt really good, but also just... really, really angry if people got in my way.
During that time when you felt unstoppable, did you believe you had any special powers or a special mission?

Special powers? No, I don't think I had like, superpowers or anything. But I did feel... I mean, I honestly believed I was about to build the best bilingual supper club in the entire city. Like, it was a sure thing. I was absolutely convinced that investors would be stupid not to back me, even though, yeah, I didn't have a job anymore or any money lined up. But the vision was just so clear. We were going to have this fusion menu, half authentic Oaxacan, half modern French. I actually tried making this mole sauce from scratch one night at like 3 AM. The recipe called for, like, twenty different ingredients, and I had to go to this 24-hour grocery store on the other side of town to find the right kind of dried chilies. The guy working the register looked so tired, he was just staring at his phone watching these weird TikToks of people power-washing driveways. It's crazy how satisfying those videos are, honestly. I could watch them for hours. There's this one guy who does it in reverse, so it looks like he's painting the dirt on... but yeah, I just knew my supper club was going to be massive. I was a genius for coming up with it.
During that time when you felt unstoppable, did you need much less sleep than usual?

Sleep? Oh, yeah. I mean, I wasn't really sleeping at all. Like, maybe an hour or two a night, tops? But I didn't even feel tired. It was crazy. Usually, if I don't get at least seven hours, I'm practically a zombie the next day. Like, when I was working at the restaurant, if I had the closing shift and then had to open the next morning, I'd be downing espresso shots just to function. The espresso machine there was this massive, shiny Italian thing, but it was always breaking down. The steam wand was super finicky. You had to hold the milk pitcher at this exact angle or it would just screech at you. My coworker, Dave, used to make these incredible latte art designs—like swans and stuff—but he was super pretentious about it. He wouldn't even let anyone else touch the machine if he was on shift. He actually got really mad at me once because I used his special tamper. It's like, dude, we're serving coffee to people in a rush, not curing diseases, you know? He was always talking about opening his own roastery someday, but he spent all his money on vintage vinyl records. He had this huge collection of 80s synth-pop... wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, sleep. Yeah, I wasn't really sleeping, but I felt totally fine. Like I had all the energy in the world.
Now that you feel slowed down, do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or send you special messages?

Harm me? No, I don't... no one's trying to hurt me. I mean, I feel awful right now, like I can barely get out of bed, but it's not because someone is doing it to me. And messages? No, definitely not. Although, speaking of messages, my phone has been blowing up with these spam texts lately. Like, constantly. They always say something about a package that couldn't be delivered, and they have these weird links. I almost clicked one the other day because I actually was waiting on a package. I ordered this heavy blanket, like a weighted one? I read online that they're supposed to help when you feel anxious or depressed, which I definitely do right now. The shipping company they use is terrible, though. Last time I ordered something from them, they left it out in the rain, and the cardboard was completely dissolved by the time I got home. The delivery guy didn't even put it on the porch, just right at the end of the driveway. My neighbor's dog actually came over and started sniffing it. It's a golden retriever, super friendly, but it sheds everywhere. The owners just let it wander around the neighborhood without a leash, which honestly seems a little irresponsible because cars speed down our street all the time... but yeah, no, no secret messages or people trying to hurt me. Just feeling really, really down.
Before this current crash, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt very depressed like this?

Have I felt this depressed before? Um... I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days, sure, but nothing like this where I just feel... empty. Like I'm moving through molasses. Usually, if I'm having a bad day, I just try to pick up an extra shift at the restaurant to stay busy. Being a waiter is exhausting, but it keeps your mind off things, you know? Plus, the tips can be decent on weekends. Although, lately, people have been tipping horribly. I had this one table last week—or maybe it was a month ago, time is kind of a blur right now—but they ran me ragged. They kept sending their drinks back, asking for extra lemons, extra napkins, complaining that the music was too loud. The music there *is* too loud, honestly. The manager insists on playing this weird electro-swing playlist on repeat. It's like, who even listens to electro-swing anymore? It's so jarring. One of the speakers is blown out right above my section, so it just rattles constantly with the bass. I told the manager about it, but he just brushed me off. He's always in the back office playing fantasy football. He takes it so seriously, like he's actually managing an NFL team or something. He even has this whiteboard where he tracks everyone's stats... wait, what was I talking about? Oh, right, being depressed. But yeah, no, I've never felt this bad before. This is completely new and it just sucks.
Before this recent period, had you ever had another time in your life when you felt unusually energized and needed very little sleep like that?

Another time feeling that energized? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, that whole thing where I wasn't sleeping and felt like I could do anything, that was the first time that ever happened. I usually need my sleep. Like I was saying about the restaurant, if I don't sleep, I'm useless. Especially when they put me on the patio section. The patio is the worst because the tables are so far from the kitchen, and you have to carry these massive trays of food out there. Last summer, we had this horrible heatwave, and the patio umbrellas barely did anything. People would sit out there and complain about the heat, like I could control the weather or something. And the bees! There were always so many bees around the sweet tea pitchers. One time, a bee actually flew into this lady's glass, and she completely freaked out. She demanded a whole new meal, not just a new drink, because she said the bee had "contaminated the airspace" around her food. Can you believe that? My manager actually gave it to her, too. He always caves to the customers, no matter how ridiculous they are. It makes us servers look like idiots when we try to enforce the rules and then he just comes over and gives them whatever they want. It's so frustrating... but yeah, no, before this recent thing, I've never had a time where I was just buzzing with energy and not sleeping like that. It was definitely a first.
Right now, do you feel guilty about something you believe you deserve to be punished for?

Guilty? No, I don't... I mean, I feel terrible, just heavy and useless, but I don't feel like I did something wrong that I need to be punished for. I haven't done anything. I can barely do anything at all. Though, speaking of doing things wrong, I did accidentally drop a whole tray of water glasses at work right before I stopped going in. It was a disaster. The ice went everywhere, and it was right in the middle of the dinner rush. This one guy slipped on a cube of ice and almost went down hard. He caught himself on a chair, but he was so mad. He was wearing these really expensive-looking loafers, the kind with the little tassels on them? I always wonder who actually buys shoes with tassels. They look so impractical, especially if you have a cat. My old roommate had a cat that would attack anything that dangled. Shoelaces, hoodie strings, you name it. One time it actually shredded the bottom of our shower curtain because it had this fringe on it. We had to go to Target and buy a new one, but they only had this ugly frosted plastic kind left. It smelled like chemicals for a week... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling guilty. But no, I don't feel like I need to be punished or anything. Just really, really drained.
Right now, do you hear voices when no one is there speaking?

Voices? No, no, I don't hear anything like that. It's actually been really quiet lately because I haven't been leaving my apartment. The only thing I hear is the radiator. It makes this awful hissing sound, especially at night when the building cranks up the heat. It's an old building, you know? Like, pre-war or something. The floors creak if you just look at them wrong. The guy who lives above me, I swear he must pace around in combat boots at 3 AM. Thump, thump, thump. I don't know what he does for a living, but he has the weirdest hours. Sometimes I smell cabbage cooking up there, too. Who cooks cabbage in the middle of the night? It seeps right through the vents. My mom used to make stuffed cabbage when I was a kid, but she used this sweet tomato sauce that made it bearable. She always made way too much, though, so we'd be eating leftovers for a week. By day four, it just turns to mush. I can't even look at cabbage now without feeling slightly nauseous... wait, what was the question? Voices, right. No, no voices. Just the radiator and the heavy walker upstairs.
Right now, do you believe you are dead or that your body is shutting down?

Dead? Shutting down? No, no, I don't think I'm dead. I mean, I feel like a zombie most days, just totally wiped out, but I know I'm alive. My body feels heavy, like I'm dragging weights around, but it's not shutting down or anything. It's just so hard to move. Speaking of moving, my car is still parked on the street because I haven't had the energy to move it for street sweeping. I'm probably racking up so many tickets. The parking enforcement in my neighborhood is ruthless. They drive these little white carts with flashing yellow lights, and they will literally wait at the end of the block until the clock strikes 8 AM, and then they just pounce. It's like a game to them. I got a ticket once because my bumper was maybe two inches into the red zone. Two inches! And the curb wasn't even painted clearly, it was all chipped and faded. I tried to contest it online, but the website is a nightmare to navigate. It looks like it was built in 1998 and never updated. You have to click through all these endless menus, and half the links are broken. I spent an hour trying to upload a picture of the faded curb, and then the page just timed out and erased everything. I was so mad I just paid the $65. It's a total scam, honestly... but anyway, no, I don't think I'm dead or anything like that. Just really, really tired.
Right now, do you believe you are worthless?

Worthless? I mean... I feel pretty useless right now, like I said, just heavy and not doing anything. But I wouldn't say worthless, exactly. Like, I still have value as a person, I guess. I just can't seem to tap into it. It's like having a gift card that you know has money on it, but you keep forgetting to bring it to the store. I have this one gift card to a coffee shop that's been in my wallet for like two years. It's for this place downtown that makes these really elaborate pour-overs. They take like ten minutes just to make one cup of coffee, and they weigh the beans on this tiny little digital scale. It's almost like a science experiment. The barista wears a leather apron and has this perfectly waxed mustache. I always wonder how much time he spends on that mustache every morning. Like, does he use a special comb? My grandfather used to have a mustache, but it was just kind of bushy and wild. He smoked a pipe, too, so it always smelled like cherry tobacco. He used to sit on the porch for hours just puffing on that pipe and watching the cars go by. He lived on this really busy street, so there were always cars. Sometimes you'd see a really cool vintage car, like an old Mustang or something, and he'd point it out with the stem of his pipe. He knew all the models and years... wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, worthless. Yeah, no, I don't think I'm worthless. Just... stuck.
Right now, do you believe people would be better off without you?

Better off without me? No, I don't think so. I mean, I know I'm not exactly the life of the party right now, and I haven't picked up a shift at the restaurant in weeks, but I don't think anyone would be better off if I was just gone. My manager at the restaurant has actually been texting me, asking when I'm coming back. We work at this diner that's open 24/7, and they're always short-staffed on the graveyard shift. It's wild in there at 3 AM on a Saturday. You get the whole post-bar crowd stumbling in, demanding cheese fries and milkshakes. We have this one milkshake machine that is notoriously temperamental. If you don't clean the spindle exactly right, it just sprays ice cream everywhere. I got it all over my uniform once right at the start of a double shift. Smelled like sour vanilla for fourteen hours. The uniforms are these terrible polyester blend button-downs, too, so they don't breathe at all. In the summer, the kitchen gets up to like a hundred and ten degrees. The grill cook, Hector, he wears this cooling towel around his neck, but I don't think it does much. He makes the best hash browns, though. Crispy on the outside, soft on the inside. He uses a ridiculous amount of butter, which is probably the secret. I tried making them at home once, but they just turned into a greasy, burnt mess in my pan. I probably need a cast-iron skillet, but those things are so heavy to wash... sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right. No, I don't think people would be better off without me. I just need to get back on my feet.
Right now, do you believe you have committed an unforgivable sin?

An unforgivable sin? No, definitely not. I mean, I'm not a perfect person, I've made mistakes, but nothing unforgivable. The worst thing I've probably done is just... I don't know, dropping a whole tray of drinks at work once. It was like six of those huge heavy glass goblets full of iced tea, just shattered right in the middle of the dining room. The sound was deafening, the whole restaurant went dead silent. 

And the ice just goes everywhere, sliding under all the booths. Sweeping up ice is the absolute worst because it melts into the floor dirt and makes this gross gray sludge. Plus, the main broom at the diner is completely useless. The bristles are all permanently bent to one side because people just shove it in the closet instead of hanging it on the hook. There's a hook literally right there on the wall next to the mop sink! It takes two seconds to hang it up. But no one does. It's exactly like how the day shift never refills the receipt paper in the register. They'll just let it run out right before the dinner rush, and then you're standing there trying to pry the plastic roller open with greasy hands while a table is staring at you waiting to pay. The plastic on those machines is so cheap, I actually snapped a piece off one time trying to force a new paper roll in. I just kind of taped it back together with clear tape and didn't tell the manager. I guess that was kind of bad, but... wait, sorry. What did you ask me? A sin? No, no, I haven't done anything unforgivable. Just regular stupid mistakes.
Are you having thoughts of killing yourself?

Thoughts of killing myself? No. No, I don't want to die. I'm just... exhausted. But no, I wouldn't do that. I've just been spending a lot of time on the couch watching TV, mostly trying to distract myself. I ended up watching this whole true crime documentary series yesterday about a guy who faked his own death by leaving his clothes on a beach. Which is such a cliché, right? Like, who actually believes the whole clothes-on-the-beach thing anymore? If you're going to disappear, you need a way better plan than that. You'd need to go somewhere completely off the grid, like a cabin in Montana or something. 

My uncle actually has a cabin in Montana. It's totally off the grid, no cell service, nothing. He has to use a satellite phone just to call my aunt. He goes up there to hunt elk, which I could never do. Elk are huge. Have you ever seen an elk up close? They look like they're from prehistoric times. Their antlers are just massive, like branches of a tree. I tried to grow a tree once, like a bonsai tree? I got it at this little kiosk at the mall when I was in college. The guy said it was super easy to take care of, just water it once a week and trim the leaves. But I guess I put it too close to the AC vent in my apartment, and the whole thing just dried up and turned brown in like three days. I felt so bad throwing it away. It came in this little ceramic pot, too, with a really nice blue glaze. I think I actually kept the pot and used it to hold paperclips for a while, but then I lost it when I moved out of the dorms. Moving is the worst, especially when you have to haul boxes up three flights of stairs... 

Wait, sorry. What was the question? Killing myself? Right. No, no, I'm not having any thoughts like that. Just feeling really drained.
Because of how slowed down and drained you feel right now, have you been unable to work?

Yeah, I... I haven't been able to work. Or do much of anything, really. I haven't picked up a shift in weeks, like I said. I just can't seem to hold any plans together. Work, rent, family stuff... it's all just falling apart. I couldn't even get my basic responsibilities organized, which is why my sister had to drive me to the crisis clinic. 

She drives this little Honda Civic that makes this awful rattling noise whenever she hits forty miles an hour. I keep telling her she needs to take it to a mechanic, but she says she doesn't want to get scammed. Mechanics can be so shady, though. I took my car in for an oil change once, and they tried to tell me I needed all four brake pads replaced, the rotors resurfaced, and a new air filter. The air filter they showed me wasn't even from my car! It was this huge, rectangular thing, and my car takes a circular one. I knew because I actually watched a YouTube tutorial on how to change it myself. YouTube is amazing for that kind of stuff. You can literally learn how to do anything. I watched this one video on how to build a bookshelf out of wooden pallets. It looked so rustic and cool. You just have to sand down the rough edges so you don't get splinters. Splinters are the worst, especially when they get stuck right under your fingernail. I got one there once when I was helping my dad chop firewood. We had this big axe with a fiberglass handle... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Work. Yeah, no, I haven't been able to work or keep up with anything lately. My sister had to step in and help me because I just... couldn't.
During this slowed-down depressed period, have you had any beliefs that other people said were not true?

Beliefs that aren't true? No, I don't think so. I mean, my sister tells me I'm being ridiculous when I say I'm completely useless, but that's just her trying to be nice, you know? It's not like I'm seeing things or believing crazy conspiracies or anything. I used to work with a guy who was super into conspiracies, though. He was convinced that the moon landing was faked on a soundstage in Hollywood. He would talk about the shadows in the photographs not lining up right, and how the flag was waving when there's no wind in space. 

He actually spent like three hours one shift trying to explain the whole thing to me while we were rolling silverware. Rolling silverware is the most tedious part of closing. You have to make sure the napkin is perfectly tight, or else the manager makes you redo the whole bin. We used these thick cloth napkins that were supposed to be white but were always kind of stained with coffee or whatever. One time, a customer complained because their napkin had a tiny red spot on it, and they thought it was blood. It was definitely just marinara sauce, we were serving a chicken parmesan special that night. Chicken parm is actually my favorite thing to make at home, but you have to pound the chicken cutlets really thin before you bread them. If you don't, they get all rubbery and take forever to cook through. I bought a meat mallet just for that, it's this heavy metal thing with spikes on one side... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Beliefs? No, no, nobody's told me I'm believing things that aren't true. Just that I'm being too hard on myself, I guess.
During the time you felt unstoppable, did you hear voices or believe things that other people said were not true?

Voices? No, no, I didn't hear anything like that. And I didn't think anything crazy, either. I just felt like I could do anything, you know? Like my brain was firing on all cylinders. I actually started writing this screenplay during that time. It was going to be this epic sci-fi movie about a society that lives entirely underwater because the surface of the Earth got too hot. 

I was staying up all night writing it, just typing away on my laptop. My laptop is getting so old, though. The 'E' key sticks sometimes, so I have to press it really hard, and the battery doesn't hold a charge for more than like twenty minutes. I should probably get a new one, but MacBooks are so expensive. My buddy Dave has a MacBook Pro, the one with the little touch bar at the top of the keyboard? It's pretty cool, but he spilled coffee on it last month and the Apple Store told him it would cost like eight hundred dollars to fix the logic board. Logic boards are basically the whole computer, right? I don't really know how computers work. Dave is super into tech stuff, he actually built his own gaming PC from scratch. He ordered all the parts online and put them together in this clear case with neon green lights inside. It looks like something out of the Matrix. 

Have you seen the Matrix? The first one is a classic, but the sequels get kind of confusing. I tried to rewatch them a while ago, but I kept falling asleep. Although, when I was feeling unstoppable, I didn't sleep at all. I just had so much energy. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Voices? Right, no. No voices or anything like that. Just... a lot of ideas.
During that time when you felt unstoppable, were you hospitalized?

Hospitalized? No, no, I didn't go to the hospital. I felt amazing, why would I go to a hospital? Hospitals are so depressing anyway. The lighting is always that harsh fluorescent kind that makes everyone look sick even if they aren't. I had to go to the ER once when I was in high school because I broke my collarbone playing intramural soccer. It was the dumbest thing, I just tripped over my own feet and landed weird. 

They made me wait in the lobby for like four hours before a doctor even looked at me. And the chairs in those waiting rooms are the absolute worst. They're like this hard plastic, molded into a shape that doesn't actually fit a human body. My back was killing me by the time they called my name. Plus, there was this guy sitting across from me who kept coughing without covering his mouth. It's like, come on man, basic hygiene, you know? I always carry hand sanitizer in my backpack now because of people like that. I get the one that smells like eucalyptus, it's supposed to be calming. My mom is really into essential oils, she has this diffuser in her living room that looks like a little wooden volcano. It puffs out steam every few seconds... 

Wait, what was the question? Hospital? Yeah, no, I definitely wasn't in the hospital when I was feeling all that energy. I was too busy writing and doing stuff.
During the time when you felt unstoppable, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life, like getting fired or major conflict with other people?

Did it cause problems? I mean... yeah, I guess it did. I haven't really been able to hold together work plans or keep up with my rent arrangements. Or family commitments, either. It got so bad that my sister actually had to take me to the crisis clinic because I just couldn't get my basic responsibilities organized on my own. It's like I had all this energy but nothing was actually getting done, you know? 

My sister is usually pretty patient with me, she's a nurse over at the county hospital. She works in the pediatric ward, which I think would be so sad, but she says it's really rewarding. She actually just bought a new car, a Honda CR-V, because her old Civic finally broke down on the highway. The transmission just completely gave out. Transmissions are so expensive to replace, it's almost not even worth it on an older car. I used to have this old Ford Taurus back in high school, and it was a total boat. It was this weird champagne color, and the AC only worked if you were driving over forty miles an hour. If you were stuck in traffic, you just had to roll the windows down and sweat. I remember driving it to the beach one summer with my friends, and we got stuck in this massive traffic jam on the bridge... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask? Problems in my life? Yeah, like I said, I couldn't keep my work or rent together, and my sister had to take me to the clinic. So yeah, definitely some problems.

Voices? No, no, I didn't hear anything like that. And I didn't think anything crazy, either. I just felt like I could do anything, you know? Like my brain was firing on all cylinders. I actually started writing this screenplay during that time. It was going to be this epic sci-fi movie about a society that lives entirely underwater because the surface of the Earth got too hot. 

I was staying up all night writing it, just typing away on my laptop. My laptop is getting so old, though. The 'E' key sticks sometimes, so I have to press it really hard, and the battery doesn't hold a charge for more than like twenty minutes. I should probably get a new one, but MacBooks are so expensive. My buddy Dave has a MacBook Pro, the one with the little touch bar at the top of the keyboard? It's pretty cool, but he spilled coffee on it last month and the Apple Store told him it would cost like eight hundred dollars to fix the logic board. Logic boards are basically the whole computer, right? I don't really know how computers work. Dave is super into tech stuff, he actually built his own gaming PC from scratch. He ordered all the parts online and put them together in this clear case with neon green lights inside. It looks like something out of the Matrix. 

Have you seen the Matrix? The first one is a classic, but the sequels get kind of confusing. I tried to rewatch them a while ago, but I kept falling asleep. Although, when I was feeling unstoppable, I didn't sleep at all. I just had so much energy. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Voices? Right, no. No voices or anything like that. Just... a lot of ideas.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the prior elevated episode caused marked impairment requiring hospitalization, to distinguish bipolar I disorder with severe mania from a milder or unspecified bipolar presentation.
doctor.question: During that time when you felt unstoppable, were you hospitalized?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I was hospitalized during my manic (unstoppable) phase, which is not covered by any of my symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Hospitalized? No, no, I didn't go to the hospital. I felt amazing, why would I go to a hospital? Hospitals are so depressing anyway. The lighting is always that harsh fluorescent kind that makes everyone look sick even if they aren't. I had to go to the ER once when I was in high school because I broke my collarbone playing intramural soccer. It was the dumbest thing, I just tripped over my own feet and landed weird. 

They made me wait in the lobby for like four hours before a doctor even looked at me. And the chairs in those waiting rooms are the absolute worst. They're like this hard plastic, molded into a shape that doesn't actually fit a human body. My back was killing me by the time they called my name. Plus, there was this guy sitting across from me who kept coughing without covering his mouth. It's like, come on man, basic hygiene, you know? I always carry hand sanitizer in my backpack now because of people like that. I get the one that smells like eucalyptus, it's supposed to be calming. My mom is really into essential oils, she has this diffuser in her living room that looks like a little wooden volcano. It puffs out steam every few seconds... 

Wait, what was the question? Hospital? Yeah, no, I definitely wasn't in the hospital when I was feeling all that energy. I was too busy writing and doing stuff.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the manic episode caused marked impairment requiring the diagnosis of bipolar I disorder, current episode depressed, severe without psychotic features, rather than a less specified bipolar diagnosis.
doctor.question: During the time when you felt unstoppable, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life, like getting fired or major conflict with other people?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I haven't been able to hold together work plans, rent arrangements, or family commitments, and my sister had to take me to the crisis clinic because I couldn't get basic responsibilities organized on my own.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the consequences of the manic phase and whether it caused serious problems or conflicts, which maps to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Did it cause problems? I mean... yeah, I guess it did. I haven't really been able to hold together work plans or keep up with my rent arrangements. Or family commitments, either. It got so bad that my sister actually had to take me to the crisis clinic because I just couldn't get my basic responsibilities organized on my own. It's like I had all this energy but nothing was actually getting done, you know? 

My sister is usually pretty patient with me, she's a nurse over at the county hospital. She works in the pediatric ward, which I think would be so sad, but she says it's really rewarding. She actually just bought a new car, a Honda CR-V, because her old Civic finally broke down on the highway. The transmission just completely gave out. Transmissions are so expensive to replace, it's almost not even worth it on an older car. I used to have this old Ford Taurus back in high school, and it was a total boat. It was this weird champagne color, and the AC only worked if you were driving over forty miles an hour. If you were stuck in traffic, you just had to roll the windows down and sweat. I remember driving it to the beach one summer with my friends, and we got stuck in this massive traffic jam on the bridge... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask? Problems in my life? Yeah, like I said, I couldn't keep my work or rent together, and my sister had to take me to the clinic. So yeah, definitely some problems.
